newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains sharply against forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains sharply against forward dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained sharply against the forward dollar on Friday after Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened heavily in the swap market, dealers said.
"RBI was in the market for spot September dollars," said a dealer. He said RBI's move caught the market unawares.
"August premia fell by 14 paise," said a dealer.
The six month annualised premia closed Friday at 6.91 percent, down from the previous close of 7.52 percent.
The RBI bought in lots of $5.0 million and $10.0 million and Friday's total purchase in the swap market should be between $75 and $100 million, dealers said.
They said the RBI was shoring up dollars ahead of redemption of India Development Bonds scheduled for next week. The second tranche of IDB redemptions is valued at about $1.8 billion.
The RBI move was also aimed at neutralising an expected shortage of rupees when the State Bank of India (SBI.BO buys dollars from the RBI for IDBs redemption, dealers said.
They expect the RBI to continue its swap transactions when the inter-bank foreign exchange market reopens on Tuesday.
Banks across India are closed on Monday for a holiday.
The spot dollar closed steady at 35.87/88. Dealers said a leading Calcutta-based bank was buying dollars at 35.88. The RBI was not in the spot market on Friday, dealers said.
